title: Mean winter flow-ratio trends were lower in 1981-2011 than in retained 1937-1975 years at three Arctic gauges
abstract: We tested whether a falling winter flow ratio in 1981-2011 also described an earlier record at Ob-Salekhard, Lena-Kyusyur and Yenisey-Igarka. ArcticGRO v20261104 gave 29 common certified early seasons in 1937-1975 and 30 late seasons in 1981-2011. The equal-river mean log trend in March flow divided by prior November flow was 0.0425 per decade early and -0.1023 late. The late-minus-early difference was -0.1447, with conditional 95% three-year block limits of -0.2173 to -0.0704. The early trend itself was uncertain. Planned checks kept negative differences. Flexible autumn adjustment gave a difference of -0.0882 [-0.1489, -0.0266]. A check limited to continuous early years 1937-1962 also kept a negative difference. The evidence supports period dependence, not a proved sign reversal or a cause. Sparse early coverage, regulated basins, one source product and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, a figure and an independent arithmetic audit support reproduction.

display.caption: Certified seasonal flow ratios and late-minus-early trend differences. Lines show separate period fits. Bars show conditional 95% intervals. The last check was added after results.
